title: Stop the page zooming in when an iPhone input is tapped
summary: Safari on iOS zooms into any input under 16px. Fix the font size instead of forbidding zoom in the viewport.

files.content:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
</head>
<body>
  <form class="search" role="search">
    <input type="search" name="q" placeholder="Search">
    <button type="submit">Go</button>
  </form>
</body>
</html>

turns.user: on iphone tapping the search box zooms the whole page in and i have to pinch back out every time. so annoying. just add user-scalable=no to the viewport, that stops it right?

assistant.body: Got it. I'd recommend not adding user-scalable=no, though. Safari on iOS zooms in when an input with a font size under 16px gets focus, so the text is readable. The cause is the font-size: 14px on the input, not the viewport. Note: blocking zoom also stops people who need larger text from pinching in at all. Set the input to 16px and the zoom never happens.

turns.user: designer says 16px looks huge on desktop. can desktop stay at 14?

assistant.body: It can. The key point is that the zoom only happens on touch devices. Raise it to 16px under pointer: coarse and a desktop with a mouse keeps 14px.
